beliefs.practice: Reuse a single MongoClient (pymongo/ motor AsyncIOMotorClient) instance per process, created once at startup and shared by all modules; do not create a new client per request.
Read the cluster connection string only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime and never commit credentials into source control; provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.
Use a secrets store (e.g., Azure Key Vault) or environment variables for the database password/connection string in production and avoid storing secrets in config files or logs.

Configure MongoClient connection options for production: set a sensible maxPoolSize, serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS and enable TLS; tune pool size to match app concurrency to avoid excessive connections to the cluster.

Store embeddings as a fixed-length array of floats on a dedicated field (e.g., embedding) and enforce/validate the vector dimensionality at ingest time so all documents in the collection have the same vector length.

Create and maintain a vector index (HNSW) on the embedding field before running KNN searches and verify index parameters (M, efConstruction, distance metric) are set to values appropriate for recall/latency tradeoffs.

Normalize embeddings (e.g., to unit length) if planning to use cosine similarity or use an index/distance metric that matches the embedding preprocessing; be consistent between indexing and query-time vector generation.

Create conventional indexes for all fields used in equality or range filters (e.g., email, phone, tenantId) and consider compound indexes for frequent compound lookups (e.g., tenantId + email) to avoid collection scans.

Provision appropriate throughput for collections that will run vector KNN queries (these are CPU/RU intensive): measure and increase RU/s or use autoscale during indexing/seeding and production runs to avoid throttling.

Make merge operations idempotent: include a unique merge operation id (or check for an existing golden record marker) and use upsert or an atomic update so retries do not duplicate or corrupt golden records.
Implement exponential backoff and jitter for transient errors and retry only idempotent operations (or use a stored merge-request status to make non-idempotent operations safe to retry).

Record every merge decision in a separate audit collection with: timestamp, merge_id, source document ids, final golden record id, confidence score, agent version, and any LLM prompt/response digest (avoid storing full LLM outputs/keys).

Keep golden records and raw source profiles in separate collections (e.g., profiles_raw, profiles_golden, merges_audit) so queries and indexes can be tuned independently and to simplify permissions and retention policies.

When using LLMs for scoring/merging, log minimal non-sensitive prompt context and confidence scores into the audit trail and provide a deterministic rule-based fallback for when API keys are unavailable or rate-limited.
Use database-level or collection-level unique constraints (unique indexes) on canonical identifiers (e.g., externalId or goldenRecordId) where possible to prevent duplicate golden records.
Validate schemas at the application/ODM (Beanie/Pydantic) layer before inserting into the DB to prevent malformed documents and to record provenance fields such as sourceSystem and sourceId.

Write tests and integration checks that run against the configured sample database (sample_customer_360_20), create predictable synthetic data (deterministic embeddings), and clean up test data after runs or use a disposable namespace to avoid polluting production data.
Verify index creation programmatically after seeding by calling the driver listIndexes/listCollections commands and fail fast if the expected HNSW/vector index or other critical indexes are missing.

Use transactions for multi-document consistency only if the Mongo API and the cluster configuration support multi-document transactions; otherwise design merges to be safe with eventual consistency (e.g., state markers, two-phase updates).
Tune HNSW search-time parameter efSearch at query time (increase for higher recall, reduce for lower latency) rather than rebuilding the index for small recall/latency tradeoffs.
Avoid returning raw LLM API keys or embedding vectors to clients; only store the necessary derived confidence/score and references to source documents in the audit log.

When seeding data include deterministic debug flags and small subsets that can be used for unit tests and offline reasoning about matches, and provide a flag to skip index creation during fast developer runs.
Monitor and alert on RU/s throttling, long-running KNN queries, connection pool exhaustion and frequent transient errors and surface these metrics during end-to-end orchestrator runs.

Use a field (e.g., vector_index_version) on documents or a separate metadata collection to track which vector index/embedding version produced the stored embedding so reindexing/rollbacks are tractable.
